ai_show_review.summary: Epic Dark Star and high‑energy set with soaring bass
ai_show_review.blurb: The Rose Palace show delivers a blistering Dark Star that showcases Jerry’s flawless tone and Phil’s soaring bass. St Stephen and The Eleven follow with tight transitions and relentless drive. The soundboard capture is crisp though the tape is incomplete.
ai_show_review.review: March 22, 1969 at the Rose Palace finds the Dead in top form, launching a fast‑paced set that never loses its lock. Opening with Good Morning Little School Girl they leap straight into an epic Dark Star where Garcia’s tone is immaculate and Lesh’s bass bomb‑like lines color every turn. The momentum rolls seamlessly into Saint Stephen and then The Eleven, each song riding on aggressive, razor‑blade drumming from Mickey and Bill that keeps the group tightly together despite the brevity of the recording. The set closes with a rousing Turn On Your Lovelight, leaving the audience buzzing. Though the tape is missing portions, the existing soundboard mix is sharp, giving clear separation to drums and bass while keeping the keyboards supportive but unobtrusive.

best_recording.reason: Sharp soundboard capture with crisp mix that highlights the epic Dark Star and tight rhythm section despite being incomplete

key_highlights: Epic Dark Star featuring flawless Garcia leads and soaring Lesh bass
Tight, high‑energy Saint Stephen segue into The Eleven
Aggressive, razor‑blade drumming from Mickey and Bill drives the set
Crisp soundboard recording that balances drums and bass nicely

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is immaculate; his leads cut through Dark Star and the other jams with precision.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass soars, providing color and a ‘bombs’ feel that fuels the improvisations.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar chimes and slices, adding extra bite to transitions.
band_performance.Tom: Tom Constanten adds subtle arpeggios early in Dark Star; keyboards stay supportive without overwhelming the mix.
band_performance.Mickey: Mickey Hart delivers aggressive, razor‑blade drumming that drives the set forward.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann matches Mickey with loud, inventive fills, keeping the rhythm tight.
